statement: The circles $C_{1}:x^{2}+y^{2}+2g_{1}x+2f_{1}y+c_{1}=0$ and $C_{2}:x^{2}+y^{2}+2g_{2}x+2f_{2}y+c_{2}=0$ meet at two points $P$ and $Q$. Show that, for any constant $\\lambda\\neq-1$, the equation $(x^{2}+y^{2}+2g_{1}x+2f_{1}y+c_{1})+\\lambda(x^{2}+y^{2}+2g_{2}x+2f_{2}y+c_{2})=0$ represents a circle passing through $P$ and $Q$.
solution:
At the intersection points $P$ and $Q$ both $C_{1}=0$ and $C_{2}=0$, so any linear combination is also zero there; hence the curve passes through $P$ and $Q$. For $\\lambda\\neq-1$ the coefficients of $x^{2}$ and $y^{2}$ are both $1+\\lambda$ (non-zero and equal) and there is no $xy$ term, so the equation is that of a circle. (When $\\lambda=-1$ the quadratic terms cancel and the equation reduces to the common chord $PQ$.)
